title: Towards In-Situ Neuromorphic Computing Architecture for Event Stream Super-Resolution
problem: Event-based cameras generate sparse, low-resolution event streams mitigating motion blur in high-speed scenarios but lacking sufficient spatial resolution. Super-resolution of event streams requires efficient neuromorphic hardware architecture avoiding excessive intermediate storage.
motivation: Event cameras offer unique advantages for high-speed capture, but low resolution limits practical applicability; efficient super-resolution is essential.
method: Designs a specialized processor using spiking neural networks—artificial neurons that fire discrete signals. The hardware simplifies neuron models, uses optimized convolution operations, and organizes processors in a hierarchical parallel array. A custom data-flow pattern called KCTR (Kernel-Channel-Timestamp-Row) with dual processing pipelines computes results directly from input data, eliminating the need to store intermediate spike values between processing layers.
key_novelty: A data-flow pattern called KCTR with dual processing pipelines that lets neuromorphic (brain-inspired) processors handle event streams directly without storing intermediate results between layers.
contributions: Hardware-friendly SNN architecture with simplified neurons and optimized convolutions
KCTR dataflow and dual-pipeline for in-situ computing
Eliminates inter-layer spike storage reducing memory overhead
95.6% reconstruction speed improvement vs GPU; 0.546 pJ/synaptic operation at 28nm, 500 MHz
primary_theme: In-situ neuromorphic accelerator for event stream super-resolution with KCTR dataflow
